description_short.value: Lithium developer building the Ewoyaa spodumene project in Ghana, with exploration licences in Côte d'Ivoire; incorporated in Australia.
description_short.source: Written by us from the Atlantic Lithium Limited 2026 Annual Report (directors' report, principal activities)

description_full.value: Atlantic Lithium Limited is developing the Ewoyaa Lithium Project in Ghana's Central Region, which it expects to become the country's first lithium mine. Ewoyaa is a spodumene pegmatite deposit with a Mineral Resource of 36.8 million tonnes at 1.24% Li2O. Its mining lease was granted in October 2023 and ratified by Ghana's Parliament in March 2026, after the fiscal terms were agreed with the government. The company also explores for lithium on about 771 km² of wholly owned licences in Côte d'Ivoire. It has no revenue yet. Elevra Lithium, formed from the merger of Piedmont Lithium and Sayona Mining, holds a 22.5% interest in the Ghana portfolio and can earn up to 50% by funding studies and development. The company is incorporated in Australia and has its registered office in Sydney. Its shares trade on AIM (ALL), the ASX (A11) and the Ghana Stock Exchange (ALLGH), where they were listed by introduction in May 2024. Assore International Holdings is the largest shareholder, with about 26% of the shares. In May 2026 the company agreed to be acquired by Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt for US$0.25486 a share in cash under an Australian scheme of arrangement, which still needs shareholder, court and regulatory approval; Elevra has separately agreed to transfer its Ewoyaa interest to Huayou. The company reports in Australian dollars, with a financial year ending 30 June.
